analysis.title: Economics Week Ahead (Weekly, November 6, 2026)
key_insights: October CPI is due Tuesday 11/10. No year-over-year rates will be published because BLS did not collect price data in October 2025 during the government shutdown, so month-over-month changes get all the attention.

Wells Fargo estimates October headline CPI at +0.28% m/m (consensus 0.3%, prior 0.65%) and core CPI at +0.21% m/m (consensus 0.2%, prior 0.33%). Gasoline inflation slowed after September's sharp rise, and food inflation likely picked up on higher commodity and transport costs.

Core goods CPI is forecast to cool from 0.25% in September to 0.11% in October, roughly the 2026 monthly average. September's apparel and toy price increases are not expected to repeat. Core services is forecast to moderate to 0.24% as primary shelter returns to trend and travel-related services fade after sharp airfare and hotel increases.
The health insurance CPI line is a watch item because October is one of the semiannual periods when its underlying source data is updated.

Even a softer core print would leave 2026 as a lost year for returning core inflation to 2%. Wells Fargo expects the report to reinforce slow, uneven disinflation and keeps its call for one more FOMC hike in December.

Existing home sales for October are forecast to fall 5.0% to a 3.79M annualized rate (consensus 3.85M, prior 3.99M). The 30-year mortgage rate reached 7.0% by end-September and pending home sales hit a 25-year low. Prices are still rising on slow supply growth, a cumulative 57% since the pandemic.
Slightly lower growth expectations should put modest downward pressure on mortgage rates, but Wells Fargo says housing is unlikely to break out of its weak state soon.

UK Q3 GDP (Thursday) is forecast at +0.7% q/q and 1.9% y/y, driven by business services, investment, technology services and AI-related spending. Higher energy bills and mortgage rates weighed on consumption.
The BoE raised Bank Rate to 4.00% this week and projects inflation near 5% by mid-2027 as energy costs feed through. Wells Fargo expects another hike in Q1 2027 to 4.25%.

Mexico October CPI (Monday) is forecast at 3.69% y/y headline and 3.84% core, with the end of summer electricity subsidies in 18 cities driving non-core prices. Banxico cut 25 bps to 6.25% and Wells Fargo expects no change through 2026 and 2027.
Brazil October CPI is forecast at 4.81% y/y, with food outweighing electricity tariff relief. Wells Fargo expects the BCB to hold the Selic at 13.75% through year-end and resume cuts in Q1 2027.

India October CPI is forecast near 6% y/y, the top of the RBI target range, on vegetable prices and base effects. Weak rainfall, El Niño and energy costs add pressure. Wells Fargo moved its RBI hike forward from Q1 2027 to December, taking the policy rate to 5.75%.

sector_views.rationale: Affordability is a headwind, with 7.0% mortgage rates, existing home sales near 3.8-4.0M and pending sales at a 25-year low.

risk_factors: A hotter core CPI print would reinforce the case for a December FOMC hike.
The health insurance CPI line may distort October core services because of the semiannual source data update.
Weak rainfall and El Niño threaten Indian agricultural output, with higher energy and transport costs limiting relief from government measures.

Mortgage rates near 7% continue to weigh on US housing.
